{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZb8T1Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDDL9E", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 85, "title": "Distinguish stable conference authors from mutable handles", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `e9d7027e71265db6ec1fdba0a5314add4a6d73a8`, `src/conference.ts:renderContribution` resolves `authorId` but prints the member's raw handle alone. Different authors sharing a handle therefore have indistinguishable attribution. Renaming an author removes the visible connection to their earlier contributions. Blank, control-bearing or technical-looking handles also bypass the conservative presentation rules already used elsewhere.

This is an existing conference presentation gap; it is not established as a regression from the latest mail merge.

## Expected outcome

Conference READ output shows the author's existing stable synthetic identity separately from their safe current pen name. A reader can distinguish duplicate-handle authors, recognize the same resident across services, and retain that recognition after a rename.

Use the existing author line, for example `発言者：(SYN-…) safe-name / existing-date`. This placement is an explicit reconstruction. Preserve the contribution journey, stored records and literal authored text.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction

Sources inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- The [author-preserved PC-VAN course archive](https://someya.sakura.ne.jp/poem/tansi/tansimain.html) identifies its SIG origin. Headers dated August 7 and 13, 1996 separate parenthesized account-style tokens from pen names accompanying titles. An August 7 notice separately identifies forum and electronic-conference publication destinations. Confidence is high in the displayed distinction and moderate in its historical interpretation. These are another SIG's later-preserved records, with encoding damage; they do not authenticate DAISIZEN conference layout, automatic name insertion or rename behavior.
- The [DAISIZEN operator memorial](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm) separately lists forums, electronic conference and OLT. Confidence is high in that preserved service distinction. Its configuration is undated, the page carries April 2026 text, and its mountain-forum chronology remains inconsistent. It supplies no conference author-header specification.
- The [まいとーく client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html) describes conference reading/writing and separately lists ID-to-handle lookup. This corroborates distinct identity/name concepts and service capabilities. Release dating is unresolved; client features do not establish target-year host formatting.
- The [earlier conference-archive lead](https://www.higashino.jp/fzero/fcgame/conference.htm) returned HTTP 502. Accessible alternatives above supported the bounded decision; no syntax or layout was inferred from that inaccessible page.

**Accepted reconstruction:** reuse `identityToken` and `penName` from `src/member-presentation.ts` unchanged. The synthetic token algorithm, author-line placement, delimiters and current-name refresh are product reconstruction, not recovered 1996 conference formatting. Confidence is high in the implementation defect and feasibility, moderate in the historical identity/name distinction, and low in exact conference geometry. Previously printed scrollback need not change after a rename. Copy no archived identities, messages or images.

### Implementation and history

`src/navigation.ts` already passes members and the historical calendar into `renderContribution`. Contributions retain stable `authorId` references in the validated `daisizen-conference` setting. `src/storage/schema.ts` rejects missing or invalid conference authors; defensive renderer fallbacks must preserve that validation.

Reproduce with a valid local fixture containing contributions by two existing fictional residents with the same handle: `13 → 2 → CONFERENCE → READ number`. Current attribution repeats the same name. Expected attribution uses distinct existing cross-service tokens. Rename either resident and reread: only the safe name changes.

Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. Conference history includes [#65](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/65), and [#71](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/71) established forum identity conventions. Completed [#83](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/83) explicitly excluded conference attribution. This handoff extends the established presentation convention without reopening those implementations.

[PR #84](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/84) and `docs/validation.md` report 287 passing checks, configured TypeScript checking/build and production mail journeys. Those are Coordinator-reported results, not checks run by this research graph, and do not validate this proposed correction.

Scope is conference author presentation and its documentation/coverage. Keep conference list contents, composition, commands, storage, seeding, AI behavior and other services unchanged. No schema migration, identity registry or new framework is needed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Resolve the contribution's existing member once and use the unchanged shared `identityToken` and `penName` helpers in its existing author line. Keep the same token namespace and algorithm used by forums, OLT and mail.
- [ ] Distinguish contributions by duplicate-handle human/resident authors. Tokens remain stable across human/resident renames, member-array reordering, reload and JSON restore. Newly rendered details show current safe names; rendering does not rewrite contribution attribution or old scrollback.
- [ ] Reuse existing safe-name behavior for blank, control-bearing and technical-looking names. Unresolved renderer references display `不明`/`名無し`, without exposing internal keys, inventing members or adding the forum-only DEMO exception. Existing invalid-reference import rejection remains intact.
- [ ] Preserve literal titles, bodies and whitespace, contribution IDs, numbers, reply references, provenance, timestamps and calendar output. Apply fallback rules only to attribution metadata. Rendering adds no writes. Preserve conference isolation from numbered forums, mail and OLT, and preserve empty/missing conference behavior.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright renderer/controller coverage for duplicate handles, human/resident renames, matching cross-service tokens, reordered members, safe-name and unresolved-member fallbacks, unchanged input records, literal Japanese/markup/whitespace and unchanged date/reply output. Test missing references directly at the renderer boundary rather than weakening valid-backup requirements.
- [ ] Include a production keyboard journey using existing helpers and valid deterministic fixtures: enter conference → read same-handle residents → contribute/reply as the local human → read → rename/reread → reload → JSON restore with reordered members → reread. Assert stable tokens and intended name updates. Verify contribution data and unrelated protected records remain unchanged by presentation-only reads; allow legitimate sends, renames and normal session/history bookkeeping. Pause automatic activity for deterministic comparisons. No real inference or model download is required.
- [ ] Preserve existing functional, storage/import/reset, consent, composition/cancellation, failed-save retry, IME, literal rendering, scrolling and terminal pacing/skip coverage. Keep ordinary conference use independent of AI consent.
- [ ] Update the conference research section and relevant README/Settings/About descriptions with source URLs, inspection date, confidence and reconstruction assumptions. Keep routine terminal output concise.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; its existing Playwright configuration includes TypeScript checking and production bundling. Record actual results, review the complete diff and affected documentation links, and run `git diff --check`.

## Optional validation

A newly recovered dated conference transcript may refine placement or spacing later. Historical screenshot matching, native-IME, hardware and human confirmation are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge with existing repository tooling.
